name: The three defects of the vessel (snod kyi skyon gsum)
description: In listening to the teaching: like an upturned pot (not hearing), a leaking pot (not retaining) and a pot with poison (mixing the teaching with afflicted motives).

name: The six stains (dri ma drug)
description: Pride, lack of faith, lack of interest, outward distraction, inward tension (withdrawal) and weariness while listening to the teaching.

name: The eight intrusive circumstances and eight incompatible propensities
description: Circumstances that suddenly destroy the freedoms (disturbance by the five poisons, stupidity, a false teacher, laziness, a flood of bad karma, servitude, practice only for protection, hypocrisy) and propensities that cut off the chance of liberation (worldly ties, bad character, no disgust with saṃsāra, no faith, delight in wrongdoing, no interest in Dharma, broken vows, broken samaya).
notes: Member lists from memory of the Words of My Perfect Teacher.

name: The sickness of effort (rtsol ba'i nad)
description: In the Great Perfection, striving to produce what is already complete — meditating, seeking, accomplishing — is itself called a sickness that obscures the nature.

name: Hope and fear (re dogs)
description: Hoping for results and fearing failure in meditation, which keep the mind in dualistic grasping; the Kunjed Gyalpo counts seeking and accomplishing among the deviations.

name: Attachment to meditative experiences
description: Grasping at bliss, clarity or non-thought leads to rebirth in the desire, form or formless realms rather than to liberation; the experiences are to be released.

name: The four ways of straying from emptiness (shor sa bzhi)
description: Straying into emptiness as the basic nature of knowables, straying on the path (seeking the fruit elsewhere), straying into emptiness as an antidote, and straying into sealing appearances with emptiness.
notes: Member list from memory (with the 'three deviations', gol sa gsum, into the three realms).

name: Mistaking the all-base for awareness
description: Resting in a blank, indifferent, thoughtless state — the all-base (kun gzhi) — and taking it for the dharmakāya; Longchenpa warns that this leads to the formless realms, not to liberation.

name: Taking understanding or experience for realization
description: Intellectual understanding (go ba) and passing experience (myong ba) mistaken for stable realization (rtogs pa).

name: The five poisons (dug lnga)
description: Desire, anger, ignorance (dullness), pride and jealousy, which lead to the realms and are, when recognized, the five wisdoms.

name: The three poisons
description: Desire, anger and ignorance, the roots of the three lower realms; in the nine-round purification breath they are expelled with the breath.

name: The eight worldly concerns
description: Gain and loss, pleasure and pain, praise and blame, fame and disgrace: the preliminaries turn the mind from them; they disqualify a disciple (Kunjed Gyalpo ch.83).

name: The four Māras
description: The demons of the aggregates, afflictions, death and the 'son of the gods' (distraction by pleasure), as obstacles to practice; cut by the kusāli offering and Chöd.

name: Breaking the samaya
description: Damaging the commitments to teacher, vajra brothers and sisters and practice ruins the practitioner (Guhyagarbha ch.9); restored by confession, Vajrasattva and feast offerings.

name: The false guru
description: A teacher without pure vows, learning, compassion or experience, chosen for fame; following such a teacher is likened to tying a millstone round one's neck.

name: Wind disorder (srog rlung)
description: Disturbance of the life-wind by forced breath practice, tension or over-effort in meditation, with agitation, anxiety and pain at the heart; the practice traditions warn against it in tsa-lung and vase breathing.

name: Outer, inner and secret obstacles (phyi nang gsang ba'i bar chad)
description: Outer obstacles from the elements and hostile forces, inner from the channels and winds (illness), secret from dualistic mind; removed by Padmasambhava practices such as the Barche Künsel ('dispelling all obstacles').

name: Harm by the eight classes of gods and spirits (lha srin sde brgyad)
description: Illness and misfortune attributed to disturbed local gods and spirits, addressed by smoke and torma offerings, ransom rites and protector practice.
